media.title: The first dragon volvelle (lunar latitude: Caput and Cauda Draconis), from Astronomicum Caesareum
media.author: Petrus Apianus (Peter Apian), with Georg Apian; printed, hand-coloured and assembled in the Apians' workshop
media.source: National Library of Poland (Polona, object 149346690), via Wikimedia Commons; public domain
media.note: The button's roundel: the paper disc and the ring of the mater it turns on, cut round on the outer rule of the printed zodiac (781.5 px on the 1600 px plate, about the mater's printed centre) and scaled to 384 px across by one premultiplied Lanczos resample (tools/face.py). face.webp is the plate itself inside that circle, the disc at home; ring.webp is dragon-volvelle's restored mater (the annulus the turning disc can uncover, restored there from the same printed signs a third or a sixth of the way round); disc.webp is dragon-volvelle's paper disc with its two tabs, CAPVT and CAVDA, and the shadows they cast. Nothing drawn or recoloured. volvelle.json is the geometry in face pixels.

credits.readme:
*Astronomicum Caesareum*, Petrus Apianus, Ingolstadt 1540, the first dragon volvelle. The copy in the National
Library of Poland (Polona), public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. The roundel is cut from `dragon-volvelle`'s own
cut of that scan (see its `assets/PICK.md` and `tools/`). The demo sets its words in Inter and Cormorant
Garamond from Google Fonts (SIL Open Font License). See `assets/credits.json`.

# volvelle-button A button with Peter Apian's paper volvelle in it. Press it and a thumb takes the disc by its tab: the printed disc with the dragon turns a few degrees on its ring of the zodiac. While the work is done it turns on, slowly. When the work is finished the button says so at once, and the disc comes to rest on the next sign. This is the button part of `dragon-volvelle` and nothing else: the inline loader inside a real ` ``` That is the full form, and the one the demo uses. Without JS it is already the finished pill: the roundel at home, the resting word, and the pill as wide as its widest word, so nothing moves when the script starts (measured in the demo: 0.00 px for every button). The short form works too, and the script builds the rest: ```html ``` `volvelle.json`, `ring.webp` and `disc.webp` must sit beside `face.webp`. ## Driving it A press starts it. The button goes busy and says its working word, and the disc turns on. Your code does the work and reports it: ```js const btn = document.getElementById('upload'); btn.addEventListener('volvelle-button:start', async () => { const vb = btn.volvelleButton; try { for await (const share of upload()) vb.progress(share); // 0..1 of the job: the disc follows it vb.done(); // the button says "Uploaded" now; the disc settles on the next sign } catch { vb.reset({ say: 'Could not upload' }); // back to rest now; the disc stops where it is } }); ``` ```js import { volvelleButton } from './volvelle-button.js'; const vb = volvelleButton(btn, { working: 'Sending', done: 'Sent', reset: 2600 }); vb.start(); // busy, no value yet (a press does this for you). false if it is busy, disabled or aria-disabled vb.progress(0.4); // forwards only; 0 keeps it waiting vb.done(); // or done({ stay: true }) to keep the done word, done({ say: '3 more scans' }) to announce that vb.reset(); // back to rest now (gives up a job: stop calling progress). reset({ say }) says why vb.state; // 'idle' | 'waiting' | 'working' | 'done' vb.loader; // the dragon-volvelle handle underneath vb.destroy(); // removes everything it added; the button is its own markup again ``` After `destroy()` the handle does nothing: a late `progress()`, `done()` or `reset()` from a job that outlived the button is ignored, and a second `destroy()` is a no-op, even after the button has been set up again. ### Options (data attributes or the options object, which wins) | | default | | |---|---|---| | `data-working` | the word | the word while busy ("Uploading"), when the label is not written in the markup | | `data-done` | the word | the word once the work is done ("Uploaded"), likewise | | `data-reset` | `2600` | ms showing the done word before the button comes back to rest; `0` stays done until `reset()` | | `data-auto` | `true` | `false`: a press does not start it, so call `start()` yourself (after validating a form, say) | | `data-status` | none | the id of an element to speak through instead of the status line the script adds after the button. Give it `role="status"` (the script adds it if there is neither a role nor `aria-live`, and takes it off in `destroy()`). Use it when the button may be removed, so its last word is said from an element that stays | | `data-turn` | `24` | seconds a turn while it waits with no value yet: 15° a second | | `data-speed` | `36` | the most degrees a second the work ever turns it. Lower is calmer; do not raise it for quick actions, which no longer wait on the disc at all | | `data-face` | `assets/face.webp` beside the script | the roundel image; its geometry and the disc and ring are read from beside it | ### Sizes Size is the class. The roundel sits concentric with the pill's round end. | class | button | roundel | where | |---|---|---|---| | `.vb-sm` | 48 px | 40 px | settings rows, toolbars, a list's Load more | | none | 56 px | 48 px | a form footer, an upload field | | `.vb-lg` | 76 px | 64 px | a share sheet or an empty state | **The floor is a 40 px roundel in a 48 px button.** Below 40 px the dragon is a pink and green smudge on yellow (see "Can you read it", below), so the CSS never draws the roundel smaller, whatever `--vb-disc` says, and the button is never shorter than the roundel and its margin. For a 32 to 40 px toolbar this is not the right button: use a plain one there. `.vb-solid` is the primary in ink. `.vb-block` makes it fill its row. A larger size: set `--vb-h` (the button), `--vb-disc` (the roundel) and `--vb-pr` (the padding after the word) on the button. The words for every state are stacked in one cell as wide as the widest, so the pill is the same size in every state and nothing beside it reflows. Each word starts the same distance from the roundel, so the two read as one thing, and a shorter word's spare room is end padding: where there is room, **make the resting word the longest** ("Sync now", "Upload scans", "Rebuild index", "Make 24 proofs") and the pill hugs it at rest. Theme with `--paper`, `--ink`, `--ink-2`, `--ink-3`, `--rule` and `--sans`; `--vb-paper` is the button's face (the demo's cards set it to their sheet colour). The parts the script adds are guarded: their geometry is `!important`, so a page's own rules (`.row span { display: block }`, `img { height: auto }`, `.bar span { width: 100% }`) cannot stretch the roundel, squash it, or unstack the words. Tested with all of those on the demo: every roundel stays round at its size. ### Events (all bubble) | | when | |---|---| | `volvelle-button:start` | pressed (or `start()`): your cue to begin the work | | `volvelle-button:state` | every change, `detail: { state, from }`: idle, waiting, working, done, idle | | `volvelle-button:done` | at `done()`: the done word is showing and has been said. The disc may still be settling | ### States | | the button | the disc | |---|---|---| | idle | its word | where the last job left it, on a sign (on first load: home, as printed, which is the ``) | | pressed | the outline face sinks a pixel and darkens a touch; the ink face lifts a clear step toward the paper instead, since near-black cannot darken much. The main mouse button, a held Space, or a touch (after 90 ms, in case it is a scroll; a quick tap shows it a moment). Slid off the button, it lets go (releasing there does nothing); slid back on, it presses again | a mouse or a held Space: a thumb takes CAPVT's tab as it goes down, and the disc turns 5° in about 0.15 s and is held there. Once per press: sliding off and on does not take it further. Let go off the button, it stays where the hand left it, as paper does. A finger takes the tab as the press lands (its click, as it lifts): until then a touch can still turn into a scroll, and the disc only turns forwards, so it could not give the turn back. A scroll that starts on the button, however long the thumb rests first, leaves the disc exactly where it was | | waiting | the working word, `aria-disabled` | turns on at 15° a second, easing in | | working | the working word | follows the work's share of its turn about 0.8 s behind it, never faster than 36° a second, never ahead of the work. At 100% it would be home | | done | the done word, at once | carried on to the next sign it can stop on calmly, and rests there. Long work, that the disc could keep up with, ends at home. After `data-reset` ms the button is back at rest | | given up (`reset()` while busy) | at rest at once | brakes to a stop where it is, in about half a second | | disabled | grey words, `disabled` (or the page's own `aria-disabled="true"` at rest) | still, pale | ## How it turns - **The word follows the work, never the disc.** `done()` shows the done word, says it, fires `volvelle-button:done` and starts the `data-reset` timer at once, in the same call: no animation frame, no timer, so a hidden tab or a stalled frame cannot hold it back. Traced at 1440 @2 (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-fix1-last/trace.py`): a 150 ms Sync, a 2 s job reporting every 100 ms, 3 s with no progress at all, a jump to 90%, and a 13 s job all changed the word 0 to 0.3 ms after their work ended, and showed it in the next frame. - **A sign at a time.** The zodiac round the disc is twelve signs of 30°, and the moon's node goes back through them. When the work is done the disc does not lap home: it is carried on to the next sign it can stop on calmly, and rests there. Quick work sets it one sign on (the 150 ms Sync: 25° of settling, over 1.7 s, after the word); a 2 s job three; long work, that the disc could follow, brings it home (the 13 s job: home, the `` again, 1.5 s after the word). It never makes a turn on its own. - **Calm.** The work's progress comes in steps; the disc does not. The button plans the disc's pace and only ever changes it gently (by at most 40° a second in a second speeding up, and 50 slowing down); the disc follows the plan on a stiff, critically damped spring, never past it, only forwards. Traced through those five jobs and a give-up: the turn was at most 36.5° a second (13 px a second at the rim of the row button), never more than 0.85° in a frame, and never backwards. A stalled frame pauses it rather than making it catch up (at most 1/30 s of turn is taken up in one frame). The press's own 5° nudge peaks at 51° a second for a tenth of a second: that is the hand, not the work. - **The press answers at once.** The first device pixel of movement at the rim came 41 to 62 ms after a mouse press (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-fix1-last/trace.py`, 1440 @2); Enter (which clicks on the key going down) takes the tab with the start, and moved it 2.9° within 60 ms (`keys.py`). A finger: the face sinks 90 ms after the touch, and the disc takes its 5° as the press lands, its first movement about 30 ms after the lift (`touch.py`, 390 @3). Scrolls that start on the button, quick or after a rest of 150 or 400 ms, and a sideways slide: 0° every time, and the face back up as the scroll begins (`touch.py`, `swipes.py`: four rested scrolls on Sync, 0° each). - **Given up** (`reset()` while busy): the button is at rest at once, and the disc stops where it is: about 9° of travel, over 0.8 s, in the trace. It does not go on to a sign, since the work did not finish. - **Off screen** nothing runs: no animation frame and no drawing, while it waits, works, settles or stops. The button works out where the disc would have got to when it matters: before the plan changes, and as the roundel comes back within a quarter of a screen of view, so the first frame it is seen in is already in place. A jump straight back into view (Tab to the button, a link, `scrollIntoView`) is painted before an observer can say so, so while a disc out of sight has turning to catch up the button keeps one passive scroll listener, and puts the disc in place before that first frame. Measured in the first animation frame after the jump (`jump.py`, 390 @3): a job ended unseen showed its sign at once (60°, where the old frame had 9.7°), Tab to Sync likewise (30°), and under reduced motion home. A job that ends unseen is on its sign when it is seen again. The same in a hidden tab. The engine does the drawing: each frame the button gives it the disc's angle (as the share of its turn, which the engine reads as forwards only) and steps the engine's own spring until the disc is there. The engine's own loop is held off, so the disc is drawn once a frame, and not at all at rest. ## Can you read it at button size? Tested by shooting the roundel at 24 to 96 px at dpr 2 and 3 and looking at it pixel for pixel (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-shots/legib/`): | | dpr 2 | dpr 3 | |---|---|---| | the dragon reads as a winged dragon | from 40 px (36 px is a winged blur, 32 px a pink and green blot) | from 32 px (28 px just) | | CAPVT and CAVDA read as two tabs (yellow pointers on the rim) | from 64 px | from 44 px | | their lettering | not at any button size (about 150 px and up) | not at any button size | So the row button uses 40 px, the smallest roundel in which the dragon reads at dpr 2. At dpr 1 a 40 px roundel is a yellow coin with a pink blot whatever the cut. **A tighter cut was tried** (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-fix1-shots/crop/`): cut just outside the tabs' tips (r 748 on the 1600 px plate, against the zodiac's outer rule at r 781.5), from the same pixels. It makes the dragon 4.5% larger, which does not change the blot at 1x, and it takes away most of the printed zodiac, the fixed ring the turning disc is read against: at row size that ring is 2.1 px wide in the current cut and 1.3 px in the tight one, so the turn reads even more like a coin going round. The current cut stays. Resting a sign on, the disc is the engine's canvas, not the ``. Measured inside the disc (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-fix1-last/sharpk.py`): at 2x the same detail as the `` (+10% and -4% by a Laplacian measure, for the 40 and 64 px roundels), at 3x a little less (-7% and -17%). Its lettering still reads where the ``'s does. At 3x, drawing the canvas at the screen's own pixels (one resample, the turn, and no 2:1 step down) was tried: clearly softer (-35% and -39%, the dragon visibly blurred), so the canvas stays at twice the screen's pixels (`tools/engine/jobs/volvelle-button-fix1-last-shots/sharpk/`). Drawing it at more than twice is crisper by the measure but grainier to the eye (it skips pixels on the way down), and is not used. ## Accessibility - A real `
